chunks: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, heard a man saying: “I am free from the religion of Muhammad.”
So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to him: “Woe to you! If you have dissociated yourself from the religion of Muhammad, then upon whose religion will you be?”
Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, did not speak to him again until he died.

key_terms.بَرِيءٌ: declaring oneself free or dissociated from something
key_terms.تَكُونُ: you will be, meaning what religious path you would belong to
key_terms.دِينِ: religion, way of faith, and religious path
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose religion is Islam
key_terms.وَيْلَكَ: an expression of stern warning and condemnation

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say to someone who declared himself free from the religion of Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns dissociation from the religion brought by the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and presents such a statement as a grave matter. It also shows the Prophet’s severe disapproval of repudiating Islam and affirms the exclusivity and truth of his religion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4310 - The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, heard a man saying, "I am free from the religion of Muhammad."
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said to him: "Woe to you! If you are free from the religion of Muhammad, then whose religion will you follow?"
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, never spoke to him again until he died.
